purpose: Sources added for the November 2026 rewrite: free-grain coverage, the World Bank's India welfare aggregate in PIP, top income and wealth shares, and HCES coverage and sampling frame.

files.vintage: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, 11 January 2023 (Release ID 1890272)
files.note: Free foodgrains to all AAY and PHH (NFSA) beneficiaries from 1 January 2023 under the renamed PMGKAY; more than 80 crore people.

files.vintage: Press Information Bureau, Cabinet decision, 29 November 2023 (Release ID 1980689)
files.note: Free foodgrains to about 81.35 crore beneficiaries under PMGKAY for five years from 1 January 2024, about Rs 11.80 lakh crore.

files.vintage: World Bank Global Poverty Monitoring Technical Note 44, June 2025 Update to the Poverty and Inequality Platform (PIP): What's New
files.note: Section 3, Adjustments to India data: URP to MMRP, PDS and free items re-valued at local market unit values, durables/rent/hospitalisation excluded, Fisher spatial deflators, single national PPP; CPHS years removed.

files.vintage: World Bank, India: Trends in Poverty from 2011-12 to 2022-23, Methodology Note (document date May 2025)
files.note: Full method behind the June 2025 India series: free and subsidised PDS items re-valued, MMRP, spatial and intra-temporal deflation allowing a single national PPP; PIP used URP until March 2025.

files.vintage: World Bank, Poverty and Inequality Platform Methodology Handbook, chapter 2 (as served November 2026)
files.note: Recall-period example: India 2011/12 poverty 22.9% on URP vs 16.2% on MMRP (2017 PPP); spatial deflation section.

files.vintage: World Bank, Poverty and Inequality Platform Methodology Handbook, chapter 3 (as served November 2026)
files.note: PPP section: separate rural and urban PPPs are now computed only for China.

files.vintage: Bharti, Chancel, Piketty and Somanchi, World Inequality Lab Working Paper 2024/09, March 2024
files.note: Top 1% income share 22.6% (highest since 1922) and wealth share 40.1% (highest since 1961) in 2022-23.

files.vintage: MoSPI/NSO, NSS Report No. 591, Survey on Household Consumption Expenditure: 2022-23 (June 2024)
files.note: Section 1.3 coverage and exclusions (floating population, barracks, orphanages, convicted prisoners, inaccessible A&N villages); Appendix B 2.2.2.0 frame (Census 2011 villages, latest UFS blocks).

files.vintage: MoSPI/NSO, NSS Report No. 592, Survey on Household Consumption Expenditure: 2023-24
files.note: Same coverage exclusions (section 1.3) and the same frame (Appendix B 2.2.2.0) as 2022-23.
